openvireo, openvireo-core origin/develop @ b56056f2e6
built with pdoc
Edit on GitHub

openvireo

OpenVireo for Python: the openvireo-core library (accounts, vaults, sync, share links, KDBX).

Everything the core exports is here: OvClient, Account, Vault, ServiceAccount, SelfHosted, EventStream, the records (ClientConfig, EntryInput …), the Host interfaces (HttpTransport, SecureStore, BlobCache, Clock, LogSink), the crypto helpers and OvError. openvireo.hosts has ready-made Host parts.

Every network or storage call is a coroutine; run it on an asyncio loop. Each takes an optional cancel=CancelToken() as its last argument; leave it out unless you want to cancel the call from elsewhere (token.cancel() ends it with OvErrorCode.ABORTED). Cancelling the asyncio task drops the call too.

Errors are OvError (the single variant OvError.Failure) with code (an OvErrorCode), wire_code, message, status, retry_after, details and server_code::

try:
    await account.login(openvireo.LoginInput(...))
except openvireo.OvError as e:
    if e.code == openvireo.OvErrorCode.UNAUTHORIZED:
        ...

The module itself is generated by UniFFI from bindings/ov-ffi (openvireo._core).

Argon2id (SPEC §3).

class CancelToken(openvireo.CancelTokenProtocol):

Cancels a running call: pass it to the call and cancel() it from anywhere; the call returns aborted. A token stays cancelled; use a fresh one per call.

CancelToken()

A token that isn't cancelled.

def cancel(self) -> None:

Cancels every call holding this token.

def is_cancelled(self) -> bool:

Whether cancel() was called.

class CancelTokenProtocol(typing.Protocol):

CancelTokenProtocol(*args, **kwargs)
def cancel(self) -> None:

Cancels every call holding this token.

def is_cancelled(self) -> bool:

Whether cancel() was called.
